newsitem.title: USA: Amoco Q1 capital expenditures $985 mln.
newsitem.headline: Amoco Q1 capital expenditures $985 mln.

text.p: Amoco Corp said worldwide capital and exploration expenditures were $985 million in the first quarter, compared with $904 million a year ago.

U.S. exploration and production operations reported first quarter earnings of $365 million compared with $281 million. "The increase primarily reflected higher energy prices, which more than offset lower production," Amoco said.

Quarterly U.S. natural gas prices averaged about $2.50 per thousand cubic feet (mcf), over $0.70 per mcf above a year ago. Average crude oil prices were almost $20.90 per barrel for the quarter, up about $3.40 per barrel versus a year earlier.

Canadian exploration and production operations reported first quarter earnings of $81 million compared with restated 1996 first quarter earnings of $34 million, excluding gains of $56 million on the sale of assets, including the sale of Amoco's remaining investment in Crestar Energy Inc.

"The operating earnings improvement resulted primarily from higher energy prices and lower exploration expenses, partially offset by lower production due to property dispositions and natural field declines," Amoco said.
Earnings for 1996 were restated to reflect certain changes in Amoco's internal structure, the company said.

Overseas exploration and production operations earned $127 million in the first quarter, compared with earnings of $121 million a year ago. "Favorably affecting 1997 earnings were higher crude oil production and prices compared with 1996. Partly offsetting were higher exploration expenses and lower natural gas production," Amoco said.

Petroleum products operations earned $28 million in the first quarter, versus restated earnings of $62 million. The 1996 earnings, previously reported as $18 million, were restated to include Canadian supply and marketing operations for crude oil, sulfur and natural gas liquids, Amoco said.
"The decline in first quarter 1997 earnings resulted from higher refining maintenance costs and lower throughput, reflecting the planned turnaround at Amoco's largest refineries," the company said.

First quarter U.S. refined product sales totaled 1.07 million barrels per day compared with 1.13 barrels per day for the first quarter of 1996. Refineries ran at 87 percent of rated capacity, compared with 90 percent a year ago.
First quarter chemical earnings were $147 million, versus $240 million.
"The decline in first-quarter earnings primarily reflected reduced paraxylene and purified terethphalic acid margins from high prior-year levels," Amoco said.

"Favorably affecting earnings were higher olefins margins and increased sales volumes for most product lines. Sales volumes for both PTA and paraxylene increased over 35 percent, reflecting in part ... capacity additions," Amoco said.
Corporate and other operations reported net expenses of $74 million in the first quarter of 1997 compared with net expenses of $66 million in the corresponding 1996 period.

The energy giant on Monday reported first-quarter 1997 earnings of $674 million, nearly flat versus first-quarter 1996 earnings of $672 million, excluding prior-year gains of $56 million on certain asset dispositions.
"Amoco's performance remains strong at a time when markets for some of our downstream products are relatively weak," said chief executive Laurance Fuller.
Amoco added that through March 31, 3.2 million shares of its common stock were repurchased at a cost of $275 million as part of Amoco's $2 billion, two-year stock repurchase program.
